title: Energetics & Thermochemistry Adventure 1: Enthalpy and calorimetry
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure enthalpy with a calorimeter using q = mcΔT.
meta_desc: Chemistry — enthalpy, calorimetry q=mcΔT, exothermic/endothermic, standard conditions.
final_note: You learned ΔH = q at constant p, q = mcΔT, exo means -ΔH (releases heat), endo +ΔH (absorbs).

concepts.def: Energy to raise 1 g by 1 K

walkthroughs.body_html:
If bond making releases more energy than bond breaking, the reaction is exothermic (ΔH negative).

Examples: combustion (-2877 kJ/mol for octane), neutralisation, respiration.

Endothermic: absorbs energy. Photosynthesis, decomposition of CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (+178 kJ/mol).

Heat transferred:

q = m × c × ΔT

m in g, c in J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ (water = 4.18), ΔT in K or °C (size same).

Lab: burn 0.46 g ethanol; heats 200 g water from 20°C to 35°C.
q = 200 × 4.18 × 15 = 12,540 J.
n(ethanol) = 0.46/46 = 0.01 mol.
ΔH_c = -12.54/0.01 = -1254 kJ/mol (lit: -1367; difference = heat loss).

Symbol ⦵: standard conditions (): 100 kPa, stated T (usually 298 K), 1 mol dm⁻³ solutions.

Key standard enthalpies:
- ΔH_c⦵ combustion: 1 mol burnt in O₂.
- ΔH_f⦵ formation: 1 mol from elements in standard states.
- ΔH_n⦵ neutralisation: 1 mol H₂O formed from acid+base.
